facts.text: Serve the cookies when Willard and Rusty hatch the plan.
facts.why: Willard and Rusty do hatch the dog kidnap plan, and the cue only says when to serve the cookies, so it claims nothing false about the film.
facts.fix: Serve the pie when Willard and Rusty hatch the plan.

facts.why: Miss Crock's business is pies and a bakery in the film, and her gift to Willard is a mincemeat pie. Cookies are never shown. Renamed as a nod to the cuff links she gives him, so it still describes a cookie.
No cookies in the film, Miss Crock is a pie heiress. Renamed after Willard so it does not claim a Crock cookie.

facts.text: Kidnap the dog. Keep the cookies.
facts.why: The film is about a pie heiress, and the kids keep nothing but trouble. Swapped cookies for the pie Crock gives Willard.
facts.fix: Kidnap the dog. Skip the pie.

facts.text: Twenty years of driving her around and all I got was a pie. Tonight I'm eating the whole thing myself.
facts.why: Willard does get cuff links and a pie, but no source gives twenty years. His family has served her for generations.
facts.fix: Years of driving her around and all I got was a pie. Tonight I'm eating the whole thing myself.

vibe.verdict: Good takeaway setting with Muffin, Rusty's lamp and the kids stealing the briefcase, but the cookie angle is shaky and the phone number runs off its box.
